I'm sorry you've been left waiting on this. Let's get it moving.

Sorry you're still down. "No ASIC chips detected" on a DC02 is usually power, not a dead board: unplug it, reseat the PSU barrel/connector firmly at both ends, and power it back up on a known-good outlet. A weak or failing PSU is the most common cause we see.

What's the email on Shop····? I'll pull the order and check your warranty route while you try that.
power is not the issue.

Understood. Then it reads like a dead hashboard, and that's an RMA, not something you should keep poking at.

Was the unit ever overclocked or reflashed? Modified units aren't covered.

Fastest help right now is our Discord, https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf, post there and mention @nullhashrate (JD). I've also put this in front of JD here.
